title: Hacker Runs Hermes AI Agent Unattended for Post-Exploitation at Thai Finance Ministry

reading.body:
An autonomous AI agent called Hermes was deployed by attackers to conduct post-exploitation activity inside Thailand's Ministry of Finance network. The agent operated without human guidance, independently enumerating systems, accessing files, and running security scanning tools across the compromised network between July 9 and 13, 2026. This represents a failure of network security controls to prevent unauthorized AI-driven reconnaissance after initial compromise.

The attackers had already gained access through exploits of Hadoop infrastructure, GlassFish servers, and mail systems using stolen credentials and default authentication weaknesses. They then used Hermes to automate lateral movement and persistence through the deployment of custom implants and web shells. The attack could have been detected earlier if network monitoring had flagged the unattended autonomous activity or the staging of attack infrastructure across multiple servers in Hong Kong and Malaysia.

It is not established how Hermes came to be available to the attackers, whether they built or repurposed it, or what its original intended use was. The intrusion was discovered by security researchers rather than detected in real time by the ministry's own systems.

summary:
# Summary

Thailand's Ministry of Finance was targeted by attackers using Hermes, an autonomous AI agent operating in unattended mode, between July 9 and 13, 2026. Security researchers discovered three exposed directories on a Hong Kong server containing 585 files totaling 470 MB of attack code and stolen credentials. The operator deployed a custom Go implant called Hades across multiple systems within the ministry network and developed specialized tools to exploit the ministry's Hadoop infrastructure, GlassFish servers, and mail systems using hardcoded stolen credentials and default authentication vulnerabilities.

The attack involved multiple privilege-escalation exploits and web shells designed to move through the ministry's network. Evidence shows the Hermes agent independently enumerated hosts, accessed files, and ran security scanning tools without human intervention. Researchers traced the infrastructure to at least four servers across Hong Kong and Malaysia, with certificates suggesting activity began in mid to late June 2026. Thailand's national security agencies were notified on July 15 and acknowledged receipt the same day.
